note: Quick guides: one-screen answers to 'How do I…'. ONE source of truth. The app (app/ui/quickguides.js via /api/guide and guide-pages.json), Flint's knowledge base (server/flintkb.js) and the website (site/quick-guides.json, written by scripts/dev/site-quick.js) all read this file. Each card: 3 to 5 steps, 60 to 120 words, one 'do' (Do it for me) and one 'show' (Show me). 'do' is runner:arg (next, help, go, settings, call, click, ask, path). 'show' is { lesson } (app/ui/flintlessons.js) or { go | settings, sel, say }. 'needs' names a window global: without it the card is not listed. {tokens} in steps come from 'labels' (the live control's own words when it is on screen, else the text here).

guides.title: Start a project
guides.intro: A project is one thing you are making, with its own chat, tasks and files. You end with an open project and a first step.
steps: Press the plus in the left rail.
Pick what you are making: a website, a game, an app or something else.
Give it a name. You can change it later.
The project opens with a first step waiting for you.

guides.title: Write down the idea
guides.intro: One or two clear sentences keep everyone, people and AI helpers alike, building the same thing. You end with a saved idea on the front page.
asks: say what the project is for
steps: Open your project.
Say what it is and who it is for, in one or two sentences.
Save it. Friends and AI helpers read this before they build.
Change it any time the idea changes.

show.say: The idea lives on the project's front page.

guides.title: See what to do next
guides.intro: When you are not sure what to do, TribeCode looks at your project and picks one useful step, so you never face a blank page.
steps: Press the ? in the top bar.
Choose What should I do next?
You get one step for where this project is, and why.
Press the button to do it, or Not now for a different one.

show.say: Help and your next step are always here.

guides.title: Take the tour
guides.intro: A two minute look around, so you know where chat, tasks, files and design live before you start making something.
steps: Press the ? in the top bar, then Learn.
Choose Take the tour with Flint.
Flint flies to each main place and says what it is for.
Tap anywhere to stop. You can run it again any time.

guides.title: Invite a friend
guides.intro: Friends join with one link, on a laptop or a phone. You end with their name in your group, ready to chat and build.
asks: add a friend to my group
share the link with a friend
steps: Press {invite} in the sidebar.
Copy the link, or show the QR code.
Send it any way you like: text, email, chat.
Your friend opens it, picks a name and is in. No account needed.

guides.title: Join from a phone
guides.intro: TribeCode works on a phone like an app, with nothing to install from a store. You end with its icon on the Home Screen.
steps: On the computer, open the invite and show the QR code.
Point the phone's camera at it and tap the link.
Pick a name and tap Join.
Tap Add to Home Screen so it opens like an app.

guides.title: Message one person
guides.intro: Use a private message when something is only for one friend and not for the whole group. It works the same way for AI helpers, and you can come back to it later.
steps: Open People in the top bar.
Click the person you want.
Choose Message. Only the two of you see it.
Your messages stay under Chat.

guides.title: Set who can do what
guides.intro: Roles decide who may change settings, who may build and who may only look. Set them when new people join your group, so everyone has the right access.
steps: Open People in the top bar.
Click a person, then choose their role.
Admins can change settings. Members can build. Guests can look and chat.
The change applies right away.

guides.title: Bring your own AI
guides.intro: Use the AI you already have, such as Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Gemini or Cursor. You end with it listed beside your friends, ready for a task.
steps: Press {ai}.
Pick the AI you already use.
Copy the one line it shows and paste it into that AI.
The AI joins like a friend, with your access and never more.

guides.title: Ask Flint to do something
guides.intro: Flint is the helper built into TribeCode. It works with no AI account at all and runs on your own device.
steps: Click Flint's box at the bottom of the sidebar.
Type what you want in plain words: add a task to fix the menu.
Flint does it, or asks one short question first.
Say undo if it was not what you meant.

show.say: Flint is here. Type in plain words.

guides.title: Make Flint smarter on this device
guides.intro: A small free download lets Flint understand what you mean, not only exact commands. It stays on your computer and works offline.
steps: Open Flint's page.
Look at On this device: it shows what your computer can run.
Choose the small download if it is offered.
Flint then understands by meaning, with nothing sent anywhere.

guides.title: See what the AI helpers are doing
guides.intro: AI helpers work in the open, so you can always see what each one is doing and stop anything you do not want.
asks: what is the ai working on
steps: Open AI helpers in the sidebar.
Each helper shows what it is working on right now.
Click one to see its changes and anything waiting for your yes.
Costly or public actions always wait for a person.

guides.title: Make a website
guides.intro: You can have a good looking page in a few minutes without writing code. You end with a site you can see in the preview.
steps: Open Website templates.
Pick one, or tell Flint what the site is for.
Click any words in the preview and type over them.
Add a block from the left when you need a new section.

guides.title: Change words and pictures on your site
guides.intro: Everything on the page can be changed by clicking it, so the site says what you want in your own words and pictures.
steps: Open the website designer.
Click the words and type. Click a picture to swap it.
Click a button to choose where it goes.
Every change is saved. Ctrl Z takes the last one back.

guides.title: Design a screen, poster or logo
guides.intro: Design is for anything visual. What you draw is made of layers, so every part can be changed later by you or by Flint.
steps: Open Design.
Pick what you are making: a screen, slides, a poster, a logo.
Choose a template or describe it to Flint.
Select anything and say what to change: make it dark.

guides.title: Start a game
guides.intro: A starter gives you a small game that already plays, so you learn by changing it. You end with something you can play.
steps: Start a project and choose Game.
Pick a starter so you have something that already runs.
Open the preview and play it.
Change one thing at a time: the hero, the level, the speed.

guides.title: See it running
guides.intro: The preview shows your site, app or game working live beside your work, so you see every change as soon as it is made.
steps: Open the preview beside your work.
Click around the way a visitor would.
Switch between App and Website at the top.
If something looks wrong, tell Flint or your AI helper what you saw.

guides.title: Add files and docs
guides.intro: Files holds everything the project knows: notes, sheets, pictures and code. Put things here so friends and helpers can use them.
steps: Open Files in the sidebar.
Drag a file or a folder onto the window.
Or press New doc to write one here.
AI helpers read what is in Files before they build.

guides.title: Collect inspiration
guides.intro: A board of things you like gives your project a look of its own. You end with colors and fonts picked from your own taste.
steps: Open the inspiration board.
Drop in pictures, links, sounds or fonts you like.
TribeCode reads the colors and suggests a look.
Say use my board's style to apply it to your site or design.

guides.title: Add a tool or widget
guides.intro: The Marketplace has free add-ons made by other people: widgets, skills, art packs and connections to other apps. You end with a new tool in your project.
steps: Open the Marketplace.
Search for what you need.
Press Add. It shows where it came from and its license.
Undo removes it. Installed lists what you have.

guides.title: Publish it
guides.intro: Publishing puts your site on the internet so anyone with the address can see it. You end with a link you can send to people, and you stay in control of it.
steps: Open Publish.
Check the name and the short description.
Press Publish. You get a web address to share.
Publish again any time to update what people see.

show.say: Publish from your project's front page.

guides.title: Check it before you publish
guides.intro: A quick check before you publish catches the small things visitors notice first. You end with a clean list, ready to go public.
steps: Open the check from your next step.
It looks for broken links, missing pictures and private things left in.
Fix what it lists, or ask Flint to fix it.
Run it again until it is clear.

guides.title: Download your site as a file
guides.intro: Your site is yours. You can take it out of TribeCode as plain files at any time and put it anywhere you like.
asks: save my website to my computer
get a zip of my site
steps: Open the website designer.
Press Download HTML for one file that works anywhere.
Or open the menu beside it for a zip with every page.
Put the file on any web service you like.

guides.title: Share a preview before it is public
guides.intro: Show a few people your work before the whole world sees it, and get their thoughts while it is still easy to change.
asks: let a friend try it first
steps: Open the preview.
Ask Flint: share the preview.
Send the link to the people you choose.
It shows your work as it is now. Publishing is still a separate step.

guides.title: Make it a phone app
guides.intro: Your project can open on a phone like an app, on Android and iPhone alike, with its own icon. No store account is needed to try it.
asks: install my app on a phone
steps: Open your project's settings.
Turn on Phone app mode.
Open the preview and choose the phone view.
Friends open the link on a phone and tap Add to Home Screen.

guides.title: Back up everything
guides.intro: A backup is one file that holds your whole group. Make one before big changes, and from time to time, so that nothing you made can ever be lost.
steps: Open Settings, then {backuptab}.
Press Download backup.
You get one file with every project, doc and message.
Keep it somewhere safe, like another drive.

guides.title: Undo a mistake
guides.intro: Almost everything can be taken back, so try things freely. You end exactly where you were before the change, with nothing lost along the way.
steps: Press Ctrl Z right after the change.
Or tell Flint: undo.
Flint says what it took back.
For anything older, open an earlier version instead.

guides.title: Go back to an older version
guides.intro: TribeCode keeps saved moments of your project as you work, so you can look back in time and return to one.
steps: Open Versions for your project.
Pick a moment from the list to see what changed.
Press Restore to go back to it.
Nothing is lost: today's version is kept in the list too.

guides.title: Start a call
guides.intro: A call is the quickest way to decide something together. Everyone in the project can talk, and anyone can share a screen while you do.
steps: Open Chat.
Press the huddle button, or Ctrl Shift M from anywhere.
Allow the microphone when the browser asks.
Friends who are online can join with one click.

guides.title: Share your screen
guides.intro: Show friends exactly what you see. It is the fastest way to explain a problem, to teach someone a step, or to show off what you made today.
steps: Join the call first.
Press Share screen.
Pick the window or the whole screen.
Press it again to stop sharing.

guides.title: Tell everyone something
guides.intro: Chat is where the whole group talks, people and AI helpers together. Use it for news, questions and quick decisions that everyone should see.
steps: Open Chat.
Type your message and press Enter.
Or ask Flint: tell everyone the new page is up.
Type @ and a name to get one person's attention.

guides.title: Add a task
guides.intro: A task is one small job that someone can finish. Small tasks are easier to share out. You end with a card on the board.
steps: Open Tasks and press {newtask}.
Say what needs doing in a few words.
Or type /task in chat, or ask Flint: add a task to fix the menu.
The card shows one button for its next step.

guides.title: Give a task to someone
guides.intro: Every task should have one owner, so nothing is forgotten. The owner can be a friend, an AI helper, or you yourself.
asks: hand a job to a friend
steps: Open Tasks.
Open the card and choose a person or an AI helper.
Or ask Flint: assign fix the menu to Maya.
They see it at the top of their own list.

guides.title: Vote on an idea
guides.intro: When the group needs to choose, a vote is fairer and faster than a long chat. You end with a clear decision everyone can see.
steps: Open the board and press {newvote}.
Write the idea in a sentence.
Everyone votes yes or no and can add a comment.
The result stays on the board so the decision is remembered.

show.say: New ideas to vote on start here.

guides.title: Put a date on the calendar
guides.intro: The calendar shows calls, deadlines and plans for the whole group in one place, so nobody has to ask when something is happening. You end with a date everyone can see.
steps: Open the calendar.
Press a day, or the new button.
Give it a title and a time.
Tasks with a due date show up here too.

guides.title: Run it like a small business
guides.intro: Company gives your project the jobs a small business has, so selling, support and money get done as well as the building.
asks: give people roles in the business
steps: Open Company.
Answer four short questions about what you are building.
Each job goes to a friend, an AI helper, or both.
A short daily plan says what each one should do.

guides.title: Ask the group for help
guides.intro: Work is where people in your group offer their skills and ask for a hand. Use it when a job needs someone else, or when you have time to give.
steps: Open Work.
Choose Get help and say what you need.
Friends or AI helpers say they are interested.
Accept one and it becomes a task on their list.

guides.title: Change the language
guides.intro: TribeCode speaks eight languages, and each person picks their own. Changing yours does not change it for anyone else in your group, and you can switch back whenever you like.
steps: Open Settings, then {looktab}.
Find Language.
Pick yours from the list.
The app changes right away, on this device.

guides.title: Change the look
guides.intro: Make TribeCode comfortable for your eyes. Your choices are yours alone, and they can follow you to your other devices if you want them to.
steps: Open Settings, then {looktab}.
Pick a theme and an accent color.
Set the text size that reads well for you.
Ctrl Shift L switches dark and light from anywhere.

guides.title: Get told when something happens
guides.intro: Hear about the things that matter, such as a message for you or a task that was finished, and stay quiet about everything else.
steps: Open Settings, then {notiftab}.
Turn on the kinds you want.
Allow notifications when the browser asks.
On a phone, add TribeCode to the Home Screen first.

guides.title: Use the keyboard
guides.intro: A few keys save a lot of clicking. Ctrl K alone can take you to any place, person, file or action in the app.
steps: Press Ctrl K to search and run anything.
Press Ctrl / to see every shortcut.
Ctrl Shift M starts a call. Ctrl Shift B reports a bug.
On a Mac, use Cmd in place of Ctrl.

show.say: Ctrl K opens this from anywhere.

guides.title: Fix "can't connect"
guides.intro: TribeCode runs on one person's computer, so most connection trouble is that computer being asleep, closed, or off the internet.
steps: Check that the computer running the group is on and TribeCode is open.
Check your own internet, then reload the page.
Ask the person who invited you for a fresh link.
Still stuck? Open Troubleshooting for more.

guides.title: A friend can't open the link
guides.intro: Invite links fail most often inside chat apps, which open pages in their own small browser. These steps fix nearly every case.
steps: Ask them to open the link in their normal browser, not inside a chat app.
Make sure your computer is on and TribeCode is open.
Copy a fresh link from the invite and send it again.
On a phone, the QR code is the surest way.

guides.title: Report a bug
guides.intro: If something breaks, a short report helps get it fixed. You do not need to explain the technical details, because they are attached.
asks: tell the makers about an error
steps: Press Ctrl Shift B, or ? then Something's wrong.
Say what you did and what happened.
A picture of the screen and the recent log are attached for you.
Send it. You can follow it under Bugs.

guides.title: Get the newest version
guides.intro: New versions arrive often, with fixes and new things to try. Updating keeps your projects and settings exactly as they are now, and it only takes a moment.
asks: am i on the latest version
steps: Press ? then Something's wrong.
Choose Check for updates.
If there is one, press Restart to update.
What's new lists what changed.

show.say: Check for updates is in here.
